entries.effect: Main menu — the button that starts a new game (German: NEUES SPIEL).
entries.note: Carries `german` only, and writing `german` is what took effect. The most corroborated id in this register, because four separate bundles wrote it over one day: the 18-id localization run, the three-component combo bundle, and twice through the mod manager, where two mods claimed the same id and the button read whichever text `gore mgr analyze` had named the winner — in both order directions, with nothing rebuilt in between.

entries.effect: Main menu — the load-game button (LADEN). Not the pause menu, which reads its load entry from a different id.
entries.note: Carries `german` only. The pause-menu half is the useful part and it was free: in a later run the same bundle changed `ui_main_settings` and `ui_main_quit` on the pause menu as well, while that screen's SPIEL LADEN stayed vanilla. So neighbouring `ui_main_` ids do not share a scope, and the prefix does not tell you which do.

entries.effect: The settings button — on the main menu (EINSTELLUNGEN) and on the pause menu, both from this one id.
entries.note: Carries `german` only. Two screens, one id: nothing in the name `ui_main_settings` says the pause menu reads it too, and `ui_main_load` sitting right beside it does not. Change this and you change both, whether or not you meant to. Found by accident — the observer sent a pause-menu screenshot while checking something else.

observations.witness: Reported by screenshot rather than in words: the observer's pause-menu screenshot showed GORE TEST 04 in place of the settings entry, while FORTSETZEN, SPIEL SPEICHERN, SPIEL LADEN and HAUPTMENÜ were unchanged.

entries.effect: The quit button — on the main menu (VERLASSEN) and on the pause menu, both from this one id.
entries.note: Carries `german` only. Same two-screen scope as `ui_main_settings`, and the same warning: the `ui_main_` prefix is not a promise that an id belongs to the main menu alone.

observations.witness: Reported by screenshot rather than in words: the observer's pause-menu screenshot showed GORE TEST 05 in place of the quit entry, while FORTSETZEN, SPIEL SPEICHERN, SPIEL LADEN and HAUPTMENÜ were unchanged.

entries.note: Carries `german` only. Seen on the main menu; the pause menu was not checked for it.

Written as GORE TEST 02 in the same 18-id bundle whose other menu ids all changed on screen, so the edit reached the game. What was refuted is that any button on the main menu reads it: the two buttons left unchanged read FORTFAHREN and ÄNDERUNGSLOG, so those come from other ids. The name is the trap — `ui_main_play` looks like the obvious id for FORTFAHREN and is not. Nobody has looked for this id on any other screen, so this is not "the id is dead".

observations.witness: Reported by screenshot rather than in words: on the observer's main-menu screenshot five buttons carried GORE TEST numbers and GORE TEST 02 was on none of them; the two remaining buttons read FORTFAHREN and ÄNDERUNGSLOG.

entries.note: Written as GORE TEST 07 in the same bundle and refuted the same way: no main-menu button showed it, and the two unchanged buttons read FORTFAHREN and ÄNDERUNGSLOG. Checked on the main menu only — the load/save screen itself was never opened with this bundle deployed.

entries.effect: Difficulty selection, the screen that follows New Game — the easiest setting (NOVIZE).

entries.note: Carries `german` only. This is the difficulty every price figure in the `item` register was measured on.

entries.effect: The apple's display name, as shown when it is picked up and in the inventory.
entries.note: Item name ids carry `german` only — no id under the `itfo`/`itmi`/`itmw`/`itwr`/`itar` prefixes has a `german_new` key at all — so `german` is what to write. This name is the display side of the class `ItFo_Apple` in the `item` register; the two are separate namespaces and editing one does not touch the other.

entries.effect: Diego's display name — the speaker name shown above his dialog lines.
entries.note: Carries `german` only. An NPC display name, not a dialog line: it changes who the subtitle says is speaking, not what is said. The line itself is a separate id (`info_diego_gamestart_11_00` for his first one).

entries.effect: Subtitle of Diego's first spoken line in a new game (vanilla: "Ich bin Diego.").
entries.note: This id has no `german_new` key, so `german` is what the game reads — the half of the language rule that is easy to get backwards after reading the journal case below. The matching recording is the voice member `german_new/OldCamp/Diego/INFO_DIEGO_GAMESTART_11_00.ogg`; subtitle and audio are independent edits and one without the other is a line that reads one way and sounds another.

entries.effect: Journal — the first Diego errand (fetching Ian's list).
entries.note: The id that settled which German key the game reads. It carries both, and a different marker was written into each: the journal showed the `german_new` one. So where both keys exist `german_new` wins, and an edit to `german` reports "Applied 1 edit(s)", rewrites the cache, and changes nothing on screen. The guide's example at the time wrote `german` only, which is how the defect was found. Checked on this one id, in German, once.
